goal: spots on the maps of «Masks of Nyarlathotep» and Pulp Cthulhu: every printed number or letter of a map is a spot that opens its place (Р-206).
extra:
## This work (Р-206)

The maps already exist as `map` records with an image (`app/<image>`, `width`/`height` in pixels) and `spots: []`. Your unit fills `spots` of its maps. Book: «Masks of Nyarlathotep» EN 7e (`masks-of-nyarlathotep-en`, printed page = physical − 3) or Pulp Cthulhu (`pulp-cthulhu-en`, printed = physical − 1); `python pipeline/source/pages.py show <book> <printed page>`.

### How to place a spot

1. Find what the map prints: numbers of its key, letters of rooms, names of places. Run `tesseract <image> - --psm 11 tsv` (upscale ×2 first with PIL for small digits; `-c tessedit_char_whitelist=0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ` for keys) to get word boxes; centre of a box → `x` = 100·cx/width, `y` = 100·cy/height (2 decimals). Then **check every spot by eye**: crop the image around it (PIL) and read the crop — OCR misses and misreads; a number OCR did not find is located by looking at the crops of the map (split into a grid). A spot is the centre of the printed label, not of the drawn building.
2. `label` — exactly as printed («17», «B»); `target` — the place record; `text` — only when several labels belong to one record (letters of rooms of one building, Р-155); `note` — doubts (a number printed twice, missing from the map, map and text disagree). A number in the key but not on the map — no spot, say so in the coverage. A spot may open another map (`target` = that map's id) when the label is that map's area.
3. `spot_shape` of the map: `{"kind": "circle"|"label", "w": …, "h": …}` in percent, the size of a printed label on this map (look at the models).

### Places for every number (owner: «да, заводи записи для всех номеров»)

- The key of a map is usually a table on the city or place record (`tables`, e.g. «Ключ карты Лондона», 1–47) or text on the book page. A key entry that has a place record already → that record (add `number` to it if it has none). One without a record → a **new small place record**: `kb/books/<book>/locations/<chapter>-<slug>.json` (Masks; for Pulp `kb/books/pulp-cthulhu-en/locations/<slug>.json`), id accordingly; `name` (official Russian names first: the key tables already use them; English in `name.en`); `location_type` (здание / место / район / область), `part_of` = the place the map shows (`shows`) or its district, `number` = the printed number, `description.ru` — the key line plus what the chapter says about the place (one to three sentences, with the page), `refs` to scenes and handouts that mention it (grep the book folder for the name), `axes` and `sources` like the neighbours, `translated` where it is our translation. Keep the key table; in its row add `refs` to the place (it is a table of the city/place record you may edit in your unit).
- Do not create places for pure orientation labels (compass, scale, «To Cairo» arrows, sea names) — a spot for a neighbouring city or road may `target` an existing record if there is one, otherwise skip it and list it.

### Ownership

Your unit owns: its map records (fill `spots`, `spot_shape`), new place files with your prefix, and the place and city records of its chapter (adding `number`, key-table `refs`). Shared city records (`kb/locations/*.json`) of your chapter are yours for this work. Do not edit maps or places of other units.

### Done

`python -B tools/check.py <your files>` — 0 errors (run tools as `python -B`, not `-I`). Coverage `checks/20261110-map-spots/<unit>.md`: per map — spots placed / key entries / new places / not placed and why. No git.
